question: What does each kind of data file do with a key the original does not know - is a new key safe in a file meant for two engines?

addresses.name: ParseSkipValue
addresses.comment: Steps over the value of a key the class does not handle, counting `{` and `}` so a whole block goes by. CCountry slot 4 calls it for the keys in its ignore list. **That is its only caller in the image** (the call at rva 0xCCDF2, 0x52 into CCountry::LoadKey), found 2026-11-20 by reading every E8/E9/0F 8x in `.text` at every byte offset as a rel32 branch (reversing/scripts/loaderarms.py). So no other loader steps over a value it was not asked to read: an unknown key written with a block has the block's contents read as the enclosing object's own keys. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unknownkeys.md, section 2.
addresses.revises: adds that the caller the comment names is the only one, which is what makes an unknown block unsafe everywhere else
addresses.evidence: loaderarms.py's last line prints every rel32 branch to 0x67AC60 in .text: one, 0xCCDF2, inside CCountry::LoadKey - the caller already recorded, so the scan finds what is known. A call through a pointer, or a second caller the scan missed, would show it wrong; the scan does not decode, so misalignment cannot hide one.

addresses.name: CTechnology::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CTechnology::LoadKey(CTechnology* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **The grammar of the technology files.** A dozen keys of its own - the ones in CTechnology.hpp - and **a key it does not know is tried as a unit type's name**: that is how `infantry_brigade = { soft_attack = 0.1 }` becomes an effect, resolved through the same by-name lookup the unit files use. `research_bonus_from` reads a list, and `folder` and `activate_*` resolve against their own databases. **Corrected 2026-11-20: only a name that is a unit type is taken for one.** The default arm (VA 0x535485) looks the key's text up with StringHashFind in CSubUnitDataBase::GetInstance() +0x10; found, it builds the 0x228-byte per-unit-type object (constructor VA 0x5A3510), calls its slot 3 (Load) on the block and appends it to the list at +0x294..+0x29C; **not found, it calls CTechStatistics::LoadKey(this, parse, key)** (VA 0x5355EF), whose own default logs `Unkown token`. The lookup answers a real null, not a null object. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unknownkeys.md, section 4.1.
addresses.revises: the comment said anything unknown is taken as a unit type's name; a name that is no unit type goes on to CTechStatistics::LoadKey
addresses.evidence: Read from VA 0x535485 to 0x535608: `test esi, esi / je 0x5355E8` after the StringHashFind call, and at 0x5355E8 `push edi / push eax / mov ecx, ebx / call 0x537DB0`. A third path out of the default arm, or the found path not calling slot 3, would show it wrong.

addresses.name: CTechStatistics::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CTechStatistics::LoadKey(CTechStatistics* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **Every country-wide effect a technology can have**, one case each - 47 of them, which is the whole list. A technology writes them at its own top level, `supply_throughput = 0.05` beside its `allow` block. **`ground_defence_effiency` is the engine's own misspelling.** Eight of them the mod never uses. The list is in GameClasses/CCountryHistory.hpp; regenerate with `switchmap.py 0x537DB0`. **The default arm (VA 0x538792), read 2026-11-20**, in order: a key beginning `tactic_` (seven bytes compared) has its value read by TokenToFixedPoint and the pair of key text and value pushed onto the vector at +0x1E8; a combined-arms unit group's name (CSubUnitDataBase_FindUnitGroup, index above 0) has its value, TokenToFixedPoint, stored at (+0x5C)[index]; a key whose token OrderTypeToMissionIndex answers other than 0x21 has its value read as a block by an inline loop - `efficiency` (0x587) into this + index*4 + 0xE0, `reduction_modifier` (0x586) into this + index*4 + 0x164, any other key passed over; **anything else is logged** - `Unkown token '<key>' in <file>`, technology.cpp line 1237, channel 0x10004 - and nothing is consumed. So the 47 cases are not the whole list of what a technology's top level takes. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unknownkeys.md, section 4.2.
addresses.revises: adds the default arm, which the comment's 'the whole list' left out: three name-resolved forms and a log line
addresses.evidence: Read from VA 0x538792 to 0x538B24: the `tactic_` compare at 0x5387A0, the push_back at 0x538834, the FindUnitGroup call at 0x5388E9 with `test esi, esi / je` and `jle`, `call 0x584410 / cmp eax, 0x21 / je 0x538A43`, the loop 0x538980..0x538A3E with `cmp eax, 0x587` and `cmp eax, 0x586`, and the log record at 0x538A43 (`push 0x4D5`, `push 0x10004`). A token read on the logging path would show the last claim wrong.

addresses.name: CSubUnitDefinition::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CSubUnitDefinition::LoadKey(CSubUnitDefinition* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **The keys its switch names**, 73 of them, one case each: `active`, `air`, `air_attack`, `air_defence`, `air_detection`, `amphibious`, `amphibious_invasion_defence`, `amphibious_invasion_speed`, `ap_attack`, `armor_value`, `available_trigger`, `build_cost_ic`, `build_cost_manpower`, `build_time`, `can_be_pride`, `can_paradrop`, `capital`, `carrier_size`, `combat_width`, `completion_size`, `convoy_attack`, `default_morale`, `default_organisation`, `defensiveness`, `distance`, `extra_amphibious_defence`, `fort`, `fuel_consumption`, `hard_attack`, `hull`, `is_armor`, `is_bomber`, `is_buildable`, `is_cag`, `is_mobile`, `is_rocket`, `is_sub`, `land`, `max_percentage_of_type`, `max_strength`, `maximum_speed`, `minimum_of_type`, `naval`, `night`, `officers`, `on_completion`, `positioning`, `priority`, `radio_strength`, `range`, `repair_cost_multiplier`, `river`, `sea_attack`, `sea_defence`, `shore_bombardment`, `soft_attack`, `softness`, `sprite`, `strategic_attack`, `sub_attack`, `sub_detection`, `supply_consumption`, `suppression`, `surface_defence`, `surface_detection`, `toughness`, `transport`, `transport_capability`, `transport_weight`, `type`, `unit_group`, `usable_by`, `visibility`. Inherited by 2 classes in all. Read from the switch by reversing/scripts/definitions.py. A loader may resolve further keys as names out of a database - CGovernment and CMinister both do - and this one does, by a terrain's name (below). **Corrected 2026-11-20: a key the switch does not name is not dropped in silence.** The default arm (VA 0x5A4D13) hands the key's text to CMap::FindTerrainByName with g_CMap; found, the terrain's index (+0x8) picks a 0x18-byte element of the array at +0x54 and that element's slot 3 (Load) reads the block - a terrain's adjuster, `forest = { attack = -0.1 }`; not found, it logs `Unknown keyword '<key>' in <file>` (subunit.cpp line 346, channel 0x10004) and returns with nothing consumed. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unknownkeys.md, section 4.3.
addresses.revises: the boilerplate 'anything that is neither is dropped in silence' was written before the default arm was read; it resolves a terrain by name and otherwise logs
addresses.evidence: Read from VA 0x5A4D13: `mov ecx, [0x1A8557C] / push eax / push ecx / call 0x491E40 / test eax, eax / je 0x5A4D90`, the found path's `mov eax, [eax+8] / lea edx, [eax+eax*2] / mov eax, [edi+0x54] / lea ecx, [eax+edx*8]` and slot 3 call, and at 0x5A4D90 the log record (`push 0x15A`, `push 0x10004`, the string `Unknown keyword '`). A unit file's misspelt key producing no record, or a token read on that path, would show it wrong.

addresses.name: CTrigger::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CTrigger::LoadKey(CTrigger* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment:
**The whole trigger half of the event script language**, and the loader all 157 trigger classes inherit. One switch over the key's save token with **153 cases** (`port`, token 201, `CPortTrigger`, is the one FINDINGS-script.md's 152-row table lacks), each building the class that implements that keyword. A **leaf** case allocates, appends the child to `this`'s child list (16-byte node at +8/+0xC/+0x10) and calls the child's slot 7 `LoadArgument` with the value CToken copied from `parse +0x228` (tail 0x5C8E04). A **block** case - `and` `or` `not` `any_core` `any_neighbor_country` `any_neighbor_province` `any_owned_province` `enemy` `check_variable` `has_cb` `relation` `threat` `spy_mission_count` and, oddly, `has_hostile_spy_mission` - appends, sets the child's `is_script_block (+0x3C)` and calls the child's slot 3 `CPersistent::Load` (tail 0x5C914E), which reads `key = value` pairs to the closing brace through the child's own slot 4 - this function again for every CAndTrigger heir. **Neither tail tests the value's token**, so a block keyword written with a scalar swallows the rest of its enclosing block, and a leaf written with `{ }` ends its parent at its own closing brace.

The default arm (0x5CAD19), in order: (1) `Trigger_LoadDatabaseKey` (0x5CFD60) with the key text, the value text and `this->is_script_block` - a government position, a building, a technology, a unit type, a law group, a combined-arms unit group, each building its leaf and calling slot 7 with a CToken of class 0xF; a positive answer ends here. (2) An ideology by name (`GetIdeologies` + `CNameDataBase::GetByName`) - a 0x4C `CAllOrganisationPopularityTrigger` loaded as a block. (3) A region name (`StringHashFind_At18` on `g_CMap +0x2A50`) - `CRegionScopeTrigger`, a block. (4) A trial scope rebinding (0x5CAE62) - `CContextTrigger`, a block. (5) Only if step 1 answered **0** - which it does when `is_script_block` is clear - `Unknown trigger-type <key> in <file>` through trigger.cpp line 0x10B on channel 0x10004. When `is_script_block` is set step 1 answers -1 after queuing the pair on `this`'s deferred lists, and an unrecognised key is then **dropped without a word** (replayed later only by CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys, which only technology loading calls).

Key tokens come from a case-insensitive ternary search tree (the text tokenizer's next-token, rva 0x66A2E0, looks every bare word up in g_dynamic_tokens through TernarySearchTreeFind), so `AND`, `Or`, `NOT`, `THIS`, `YES` are the keywords. Every lookup of the key's or value's **text** in the default arm and the LoadArgument bodies is case-sensitive (the engine string hash and a byte compare), except a country tag (CCountryDataBase::GetTag compares three characters with `_strnicmp` after hashing them case-sensitively). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md. **The failing default consumes nothing** (VA 0x9CAEE3..0x9CAFA1, read 2026-11-20: the test of the database lookup's answer, the `Unknown trigger-type` record, two string destructors, the epilogue - no token read on either path), so an unknown key written with a block that is no ideology, region or scope leaves the block's conditions to be read as the parent's own and its `}` to close the parent. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unknownkeys.md, section 4.4.
addresses.revises: adds what the failing default does with a block, which the comment did not say
addresses.evidence: Read from VA 0x9CAEE3 to 0x9CAFA1: `cmp [esp+0xC], 0 / jne 0x9CAF85`, the log block, `call 0x401070` twice and the epilogue. A call to ParseReadKeyValue, ParseSkipValue or the tokenizer in that range would show it wrong; loaderarms.py finds no branch to ParseSkipValue anywhere in the function.
